_comment: Blocking findings that exist in the data today and are accepted for now, so
CI fails on NEW breakage rather than on the backlog it was added to expose.
This is a baseline, not a suppression list. Every entry names real damage in
a shipped file and should be deleted as the file is fixed -- run
`qwt.py check --strict` to see the full picture at any time. Verses are
listed explicitly so that the same defect spreading to another ayah still

missing-ayah.why: Absent from QUL resource 144 itself -- its ayah-by-ayah preview returns 'Translation is not available for this ayah', while three other Kurdish editions return 108:3 normally. Re-exporting will not fix it. Tracked in quranwise#71.

non-prose-stub.why: PREVIOUSLY MIS-FRAMED HERE as an isolated stub needing a check against the QUL source. It is not isolated. It is the TAIL MARKER OF A SIX-VERSE MISALIGNMENT, and '49.' is the orphaned ROW NUMBER of the verse that was deleted. Canonical 27:49 ('Take a mutual oath by Allah that we will kill him by night') is absent from this edition altogether. Slots 27:49 through 27:54 each hold the NEXT canonical ayah -- 27:49 holds canonical 27:50, 27:54 holds canonical 27:55 -- and the shift terminates at 27:55, where the leftover slot was filled with the deleted row's number instead of text. 27:48 and 27:56 are both correct. Verified verse by verse against en-sahih. So the damage is a MISSING VERSE plus six misplaced ones, not one bad cell: repairing 27:55 alone would leave six verses still wrong and silently hide the real defect. Same shape as the cs-czech and pl-bielawski fault above -- a row deleted, the block below shifted up by one, filler in the last slot -- though this is a Hausa edition, so if that mechanism is shared it is the export tooling and not a Central European locale. Needs a decision of its own; nothing here may be repaired by rule.
The value is '.' rather than a translation. Needs checking against the QUL source.

dropped.decision: DROPPED FROM THE APP by the owner. Do not re-add this edition without reading this entry first.
dropped.why: Four verses cannot be recovered from this file, and there is no alternative QUL resource for the edition to re-export from. The translator is unlisted on QUL, so there is nobody to ask. 30:18, 56:2 and 56:13 are the spreadsheet error literal '#NAZEV?' -- see the error-literal entry below; their text was never in the export. 17:32 is lost to the shift described next. The data file is deliberately KEPT in this repo: it is the evidence for the shared-pipeline hypothesis below, and removing it would delete the only record of what the fault looks like. The removal is from the app's edition registry, not from here.
dropped.the-shift: Slots 17:32 through 17:81 each hold the translation of the NEXT canonical ayah: 17:32 holds canonical 17:33 ('do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden'), and so on for 50 slots. Canonical 17:32 ('do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse') is absent entirely. The offset is absorbed at the end of the range by a DUPLICATE: 17:81 and 17:82 both carry canonical 17:82. Alignment is correct again from 17:83. Verified verse by verse against en-sahih.

error-literal.why: The value is the spreadsheet error literal '#NAZEV?' (Czech for '#NAME?') rather than a translation -- the export was produced from a sheet where three cells failed to evaluate, and the failure was written out verbatim. The text of these three ayahs is simply absent and cannot be recovered from this file. No alternative QUL resource for this edition exists. Accepted here so the new error-literal check fails on any NEW occurrence rather than on these three.

shared-pipeline-hypothesis.why: RECORDED AT THE OWNER'S REQUEST, AND THE FIRST THING TO CHECK FOR ANY NEW CENTRAL EUROPEAN EDITION. cs-czech and pl-bielawski break at the IDENTICAL range, 17:32-17:81, in the identical way, and that is near-certainly one shared upstream tooling fault rather than two coincidences. Both files put canonical 17:33 in slot 17:32 and carry the one-slot shift for exactly 50 slots. They differ only in how the block terminates. pl-bielawski is a PURE LOSSLESS ROTATION: the displaced canonical 17:32 reappears in slot 17:81, so nothing is lost and rotating the block back would fully repair it. cs-czech is the same rotation gone lossy: instead of 17:32 landing in the last slot, that slot was filled with a copy of 17:82 and the verse was lost. This sits alongside the other evidence that pl-bielawski came through a Central European pipeline: its mojibake was UTF-8 read back through ISO-8859-2, which is what such an export does -- see the MOJIBAKE comment in qwtrans.py. A rotation by one over a fixed 50-row window is what a spreadsheet does when a row is deleted without the range being adjusted. REPAIRING pl-bielawski's rotation NEEDS ITS OWN AUTHORISATION and is not covered by any decision so far.

_heuristics_comment: The corpus-level heuristics -- length-outlier, adjacent-duplicate and
verse-offset -- are correlations over text length and repetition. They
cannot prove a defect, only point a person at one, so they are all
severity `review` and none of them ever fails a build.
This section is what keeps them readable: `check` prints only the verses
a heuristic flags that are NOT listed here, so a run stays quiet until an
edition's flags CHANGE. Verses are listed rather than counted because a
count cannot tell one outlier being replaced by another from nothing
happening at all, and that swap is the shape of a bad re-export.
Every entry was read before it was added. Adding one means 'a person
looked at this and it is not damage', or 'it is damage, and it is tracked
elsewhere' -- never 'make the warning go away'.

adjacent-duplicate.why: Identical to the preceding ayah with no Arabic similarity to explain it. Surviving both gates, so worth a human read -- but repeating a neighbour is not by itself proof of a defect, and nothing here may be repaired by rule. See HEURISTIC_OPT_OUT in qwtrans.py.
17:82 repeats 17:81. This is the tail of the 17:32-17:81 shift -- the duplicate is what absorbs the offset left by the loss of canonical 17:32. See the cs-czech entry under `accepted`.

verse-offset.why: 17:62..17:68 by +1, the same shift. See the cs-czech entry under `accepted`; the edition is being dropped.

READ AGAINST THE TEXT, AND REAL -- and not nine runs of 73 verses as first recorded. It is damage, tracked in quranwise#113; the verses listed here are only what the length-based scan flags, not the extent. Actual extent: ONE continuous run of 196 slots, 3:4-3:199, each holding the NEXT canonical ayah. Head is a MERGE: slot 3:3 (386 chars against neighbours of 64 and 103) carries canonical 3:3 AND 3:4 fused into one cell. Tail is a SPLIT: canonical 3:199 is divided across slots 3:198 and 3:199, which keeps the surah at 200. 3:1, 3:2 and 3:200 are correct. LOSSLESS -- no Finnish text is missing -- so re-alignment is possible and authorised, but it is BLOCKED ON A FINNISH READER to place the 3:3/3:4 seam: one Finnish clause spans the canonical boundary. Do not apply the mechanical shift without the seam decided. Other ranges this scan raised (53:1-53:5, 77:28-77:30) were read and are false positives. UPSTREAM CONFIRMED (2026-09-17): a fresh QUL download of resource 127 is identical to this file in all 6,236 verses after import normalisation (only a BOM on 1:1 differs), and QUL's export is dated 2025-05-27, before our import -- re-exporting cannot fix it. Nothing to swap to: QUL has no other Finnish resource and QuranEnc has no Finnish translation. The only routes are the lossless re-align or withdrawal. The only MERGE-shaped instance found; the cs-czech/pl-bielawski/ha-gumi/ro-grigore cases are all deletions -- see accepted.cs-czech.shared-pipeline-hypothesis.
27:48..27:53 by +1. Corroborates the 27:49-27:54 misalignment recorded in the ha-gumi entry under `accepted`, of which the '49.' at 27:55 is the orphaned tail.

length-outlier.why: Not a mis-export: Piccardo's edition carries a whole commentary block on the final ayah of each surah, and shorter exegetical notes inline elsewhere, so 106 verses run past 3x the cross-edition median. 2:286 is 72,028 characters against a median of 213. Worth a decision about splitting the commentary out of the verse text -- it is a real reading-experience problem -- but it is the source's own structure, not damage, and nothing here should be rewritten by a tool.

verse-offset.why: 17:60..17:66 by +1 -- the IDENTICAL range as cs-czech, and the strongest evidence for the shared-upstream-pipeline hypothesis recorded in the cs-czech entry under `accepted`. Unlike cs-czech this one is a lossless rotation: no verse is missing, so it is recoverable by rotating the block back. Needs its own authorisation first.

adjacent-duplicate.why: Both are real damage, tracked in quranwise#112, not benign repetition. 55:10 is the filler that terminates the 53:34-55:9 one-slot shift (see verse-offset). 14:11 is an independent defect: it duplicates 14:10 byte for byte, and canonical 14:11 is absent from the file. Nothing here may be repaired by rule. See HEURISTIC_OPT_OUT in qwtrans.py.

verse-offset.why: READ AGAINST THE TEXT, AND REAL -- this flag badly UNDERSTATES it. It is damage, tracked in quranwise#112; the verses listed here are only what the length-based scan happens to flag, not the extent. Actual extent: ONE continuous run of 93 slots, 53:34-55:9, each holding the NEXT canonical ayah, crossing two surah boundaries (slot 53:62 holds canonical 54:1, the moon splitting; slot 54:55 holds canonical 55:1, 'The Most Merciful'). Head is LOSSY: canonical 53:34 is absent from the file entirely. Tail is absorbed by the byte-identical filler at 55:10 (see adjacent-duplicate). Not repairable by rule -- the missing verse would have to be invented. UPSTREAM CONFIRMED (2026-09-17): a fresh QUL download of resource 135 is identical to this file in all 6,236 verses, and QUL's export is dated 2025-05-27, before our import -- re-exporting cannot fix it. Alternatives evaluated: QUL 465 and 293 both pass every check and a word-overlap alignment test, but QUL states no licence for either. 465 is QuranEnc's romanian_project (Islam4ro.com, v1.0.4) with QuranEnc's footnotes stripped from 1,127 verses, which QuranEnc's no-deletion term forbids, so QUL's copy is not shippable. The QuranEnc original, footnotes kept, is -- fetched and stored like ka-rwwad. 293's licence is unknown. Recommended remedy and owner decision: see quranwise#112. Length-correlation cannot see this class of damage (it finds zero runs in cs-czech): treat any count here as a floor, never a measurement.
